literal: Pleasant words while existing, speaking harsh words is like choosing unripe fruit while ripe fruit is present.
translation: Speaking harsh words when pleasant words are available is like choosing to eat unripe fruit when ripe fruit is at hand.
modern: இனிய சொற்கள் இருக்கும்போது கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசுவது, பழுத்த பழங்கள் இருக்கும்போது பச்சைக் காய்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து உண்பதற்கு ஒப்பானது ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a simple yet powerful analogy to highlight the foolishness of using harsh language. The poet compares pleasant words to sweet, ripe fruits and harsh words to bitter, unripe fruits. When both options are available, choosing to speak harshly is as senseless as choosing to eat sour, unripe fruit when delicious ripe fruit is readily available. The word 'kavarntu' here means choosing or taking with desire, emphasizing the active, foolish choice of the speaker.
